summary: Prolonged client-side read deadline exceeded for requests with very large prompt + max_tokens
description:
Issue summary:
Customers are observing client-side read deadline exceeded errors (HTTP 504 / streaming disconnects) when sending priming prompts > 120k tokens together with max_tokens >= 65k. The failures started appearing after a throughput/priority tweak rolled 2026-03-08 and are intermittent but reproducible.

Impact:
- Multiple enterprise customers experience partial or full generation failures for long-context workflows (chat history + docs priming).
- Requests frequently stream initial tokens then hang for an extended period before client times out.
- Affects mission-critical health workflows at LexaHealth (delays in clinical note drafting).

Environment:
- Production (us-east) backend; traffic hits hosted API via edge proxy, routed to dedicated serving pools for enterprise tenants.
- Observed against redwood-v2-xl and v1-compat quantized variants.

Observed behavior:
- Successful first N tokens (often 800-2000 tokens), then long stall (30-80s) followed by client read-deadline and connection termination.
- Server-side traces show finalizer queue piling and per-request worker preemption in some cases.
- No immediate 5xx returned by runtime; client only sees a streaming disconnect or 504 after read deadline.

Expected behavior:
- Stream continues at steady rate until model generation completes or fails quickly with a deterministic error.

Notes:
- Customer reports reduction of failures when max_tokens reduced to <= 4k or when request split across multiple calls.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use LexaHealth test tenant request with a priming document ~120k tokens + user prompt (~300 tokens).
2) Set max_tokens to 65,536 and streaming=true.
3) Send request to api.redwood.ai/v1/generate using SDK (node/python) with default client read timeout (60s).
4) Observe initial streaming chunks then a hang; client logs a read deadline exceeded after ~65-75s.
5) Repeat with max_tokens=4096 and observe successful completion within normal latency.
logs:
edge-proxy: tcp proxy forwarded; initial chunks delivered.
serving-runtime[2026-03-10T15:12:03Z]: request id r-8b3c: prefix tokens streamed (1-1200) then stalled; finalizer_queue_length=42; worker_preempt=true; kv_cache_evictions=3; kernel_swap_count=1.
finalizer: backlog spike from 5->120 between 15:12:02 and 15:12:08.
client (LexaHealth): socket read timeout at 15:13:08, error: 'read deadline exceeded'.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Avery Chen (Support): Customer reported repeated streaming disconnects for large priming payloads; opened ticket and requested priority investigation.

2026-03-10 - Marcus Delgado (SRE): Acknowledged; initial hypothesis: recent priority rebalancing pushed heavy long-context requests into shared finalizer queue causing head-of-line blocking. Collecting traces and finalizer metrics.
2026-03-11 - LexaHealth (Customer): Confirmed that lowering max_tokens to 4k dramatically reduces failures; provided sample payload and reproduction script.

2026-03-12 - Eng (runtime): Reproduced locally with synthetic priming; observed kv-cache eviction thrash plus long GC-ish pauses around kernel handoff. Suspect combination of prefix size + large output budget causing synchronous finalization steps to queue.

2026-03-13 - SRE: Temporary mitigation applied: throttle long-context requests to lower-priority lane and force streaming heartbeat packets every 15s to keep client sockets alive. Customer notified; monitoring for regressions.

2026-03-13 - Eng: Working on a longer-term fix: batching/finalizer change to prioritize active streaming connections and introduce per-request soft time-slicing to avoid long blocking on kernel swaps.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses: 1) Finalizer queue priority inversion: large output-budget requests block GPU worker finalization path while smaller requests are starved. 2) KV cache eviction churn on huge prefixes causes synchronous I/O and kernel handoffs, introducing long pauses. 3) Edge proxy/client heartbeat mismatch: client times out before streaming heartbeats are emitted during backpressure.
Evidence: finalizer_queue_length spikes and worker_preempt flag correlated to customer failures; reproducer reproduces latency spike when kernel_swap_count>0 and kv_cache_evictions>0.
Next steps: gather perf traces for finalizer loop; add instrumentation to record per-request kernel handoff duration; run controlled canary with throttled finalizer concurrency.
resolution:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-13):
- Short-term: throttle enterprise long-context requests to a dedicated lane with guaranteed background progress; enable synthetic streaming heartbeats for in-flight long requests to prevent client read timeouts.
- Customer-facing workaround: split priming into smaller priming chunks (<= 32k tokens) or reduce max_tokens to <= 8k when possible.
- Medium-term: engineering will land changes to finalizer scheduling to prioritize active streaming sockets and implement incremental KV load/stream-friendly kernel handoffs (tracked in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/548).
Follow-up actions: add runbook step to detect finalizer backlog and auto-promote synthetic heartbeats; add metric alert (finalizer_queue_length>50 for >30s) and create playbook for traffic re-route.
Status: mitigation implemented and monitoring; permanent fix in development (target rollout 2026-03-27).
